hypothesis: A crafted `WRITE_AND_READ_REGISTERS` request with a `quantity to write` field that implies a data payload larger than the actual request length will cause an out-of-bounds read.
evidence_source: In `modbus_reply`, the handler for `MODBUS_FC_WRITE_AND_READ_REGISTERS` contains a loop from line 978 to 982 that reads `nb_write * 2` bytes from the request buffer. The value `nb_write` is read from the request itself. While the code checks if the declared `nb_write_bytes` field is equal to `nb_write * 2`, it fails to check if the actual request length, `req_length`, is large enough to contain `nb_write * 2` bytes of data starting from `req[offset + 10]`. An attacker can provide a truncated packet, causing the loop to read past the end of the `req` buffer.
input_artifact: not_available (static source review; no input artifact)
expected_behavior: The program will read past the end of the `req` buffer, potentially causing a crash (segmentation fault) or leaking sensitive information from adjacent memory. An address sanitizer build would report a heap-buffer-overflow or stack-buffer-overflow read.
observed_behavior: not_available (static source review; nothing was executed)
notes: This is another instance of the same pattern of vulnerability as in other write handlers: trusting PDU length fields without validating against the overall packet length.
